concepts.heading: Every Path to Parenthood
concepts.plain: Birth, adoption, fostering, surrogacy or joining a family with kids all change intimacy.

concepts.heading: Why Desire Often Drops
concepts.plain: Exhaustion, being touched all day and a new identity can all quiet desire for a while.

concepts.heading: Desire Can Come Back Differently
concepts.plain: For many parents, desire shows up after closeness starts rather than before.

checks.prompt: Alex has held the baby all day and doesn't want to be touched in the evening. What fits best?
options: Feeling "touched out" is common and doesn't mean the relationship is failing
Alex has lost interest in their partner
Alex should push through it to keep the relationship healthy
checks.explanation: Many parents feel "touched out" after a day of caregiving. It is a normal response, not a sign of a failing relationship.

655c79d9-437d-5935-8dcc-8652345b810f.takeaway: Lower desire after a child arrives is common, has real causes, and usually shifts again with time and care.

concepts.heading: Wait for the Okay
concepts.plain: Ask your clinician when it is safe to have sex again. There is no deadline after that.

concepts.heading: Go Slowly and Use Lube
concepts.plain: Start gently, use plenty of lubricant, and stop if anything hurts.

concepts.heading: Plan for Contraception
concepts.plain: You can get pregnant again before your period returns.

concepts.heading: Mental Health Matters Too
concepts.plain: Depression and anxiety after a new child are common in any parent and very treatable.

checks.prompt: Sex after birth is painful for Jo. What does the lesson suggest?
options: Keep going so it gets easier
Avoid mentioning it so the partner doesn't worry
Stop, and talk to a clinician or pelvic floor physical therapist
checks.explanation: Pain is a signal to stop. Clinicians and pelvic floor physical therapists can help.

checks.prompt: Sam, a new adoptive parent, has felt numb and hopeless for weeks. What fits best?
options: Only birth parents get depression after a new child
Any new parent can, and help is available, so Sam should reach out
It will pass on its own, so there's no need to say anything
checks.explanation: Depression after a new child can affect any parent, and it is very treatable. Reaching out is the right step.

6dc893ed-61be-503a-bdbc-9bfe1272512b.takeaway: Wait for your clinician's OK, go slowly, and never push through pain.

concepts.heading: Share the Load Fairly
concepts.plain: Unfair division of chores and planning is one of the biggest desire killers.

concepts.heading: Small, Daily Connection
concepts.plain: Short moments of attention each day matter more than one big date.

concepts.heading: Touch Without Pressure
concepts.plain: Cuddling and affection that don't have to lead to sex rebuild closeness.

concepts.heading: Planning Isn't Unromantic
concepts.plain: With a child at home, planned time together is often the only time there is.

checks.prompt: Maya does most of the night feeds and all the planning, and her desire has dropped. What might help most?
options: Scheduling more date nights while keeping the work the same
Sharing the work, including the planning, more fairly
Waiting until the baby is older
checks.explanation: When one partner carries most of the load, desire often drops. Sharing the work, including the planning, tends to help.

a4114dc2-ad6d-5719-b935-e1ccf27088b2.takeaway: Fair sharing of the work and small daily moments of connection protect intimacy.

concepts.heading: Talk About It Without Blame
concepts.plain: Share what you feel and need, and ask about your partner's experience too.

concepts.heading: Different Levels of Desire
concepts.plain: Differences in desire are normal and can be worked through together.

concepts.heading: When to Get Help
concepts.plain: If you feel stuck or resentful for months, a therapist can help.

checks.prompt: Which opening is most likely to help?
options: "I miss feeling close to you. How are you feeling about us lately?"
checks.explanation: Sharing your own feeling and asking about theirs invites a conversation instead of a defense.

64ae7874-bb4b-5ff7-8a50-a543a572f29c.takeaway: Talk with curiosity, not blame, and get help if you feel stuck.
